title: Pharmacies (Eczane), Prescriptions & Emergency Healthcare in Türkiye

quickAnswer: Turkish pharmacies (Eczane) dispense everyday painkillers, antihistamines, and rehydration salts over the counter, while antibiotics and sedatives strictly require a Turkish doctor's prescription. For overnight medication, look up the nearest rotating 24-hour Nöbetçi Eczane. In a medical emergency, dial 112 nationwide or go directly to a private hospital's Acil (ER).
category: Practical Travel Logistics, Money, Visas & Transport

body.text: Healthcare in Türkiye's major cities and coastal hubs is modern, fast, and far more accessible than many first-time visitors expect. Knowing how neighbourhood pharmacies operate—and what paperwork private hospitals issue for travel insurance claims—saves hours of stress if a minor ailment or sudden injury interrupts your trip.
What medications can you buy over the counter at a Turkish Eczane?

Licensed Turkish pharmacists (eczacı) can sell standard paracetamol, ibuprofen, oral rehydration salts, antacids, throat lozenges, motion-sickness tablets, and non-drowsy antihistamines over the counter without a prescription. Under regulations enforced by the Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (TİTCK), antibiotics, sedatives, opioid painkillers, and injectables are strictly prescription-only nationwide.

Brand names differ from those in North America or the UK, so write down the generic active ingredient (for example, ibuprofen or cetirizine) rather than a commercial label. As outlined in [Acıbadem International's OTC medicine guide](https://acibademinternational.com/patient-guides/over-the-counter-medicines-in-turkey-what-is-safe-to-buy/), pharmacists cannot legally hand over antibiotics without a physician's reçete (prescription)—a policy enforced to curb antimicrobial resistance ([Istanbul Medical Center](https://istanbulmedicalcenter.com/en/servisler/buy-antibiotics-in-turkey-without-prescription/)).

items: Standard hours: Most urban pharmacies open Monday to Saturday, 09:00–19:00, and close on Sundays and public holidays.

Bring chronic medications: Pack enough of your regular prescriptions in original labelled containers plus a copy of your doctor's letter, as foreign prescriptions cannot be filled directly at Turkish pharmacies.
Pricing transparency: Medicine prices are regulated nationwide by the Ministry of Health, meaning a box of paracetamol costs the same in Sultanahmet as in a residential suburb.

body.text: How do you find a 24-hour duty pharmacy (Nöbetçi Eczane)?

Every Turkish district operates a mandatory overnight and Sunday rotation of 24-hour duty pharmacies called Nöbetçi Eczane. You can find the closest open branch by checking the illuminated digital sign posted in any closed pharmacy's front window, searching the official [e-Devlet / TİTCK Duty Pharmacy Locator](https://www.turkiye.gov.tr/saglik-titck-nobetci-eczane-sorgulama), or checking the [Istanbul Chamber of Pharmacists](https://www.istanbuleczaciodasi.org.tr/).

After 19:00, a Nöbetçi Eczane locks its main door and serves customers through a small street-facing service window (nöbet penceresi) with a doorbell. In Istanbul, Bodrum, and Antalya, hotel receptionists also keep the nightly duty list on hand and can call ahead to confirm stock before you take a taxi.
What emergency numbers (112) and English-speaking hospitals exist?

Türkiye uses 112 as its unified, toll-free national emergency number for ambulance, police, and fire services, operating 24/7 with English-speaking dispatchers available ([Acıbadem International Emergency Guide](https://acibademinternational.com/patient-guides/emergency-contacts-for-medical-travelers-in-turkey/)). For urgent non-life-threatening care in Istanbul, private hospitals maintain dedicated international patient desks with fluent English coordinators.

body.text: Always carry your passport (or a clear photo plus your physical passport when heading to a hospital), as Turkish private hospitals require passport registration to open a medical chart.
How does travel insurance reimbursement work at private Turkish hospitals?

Most outpatient and minor ER visits at private Turkish hospitals work on a pay-and-claim basis: pay by card at discharge and submit the English medical report and itemised bill to your insurer. For hospital admissions or major procedures, call your insurer's 24/7 line to request a Guarantee of Payment (GOP) for direct billing.
Before leaving the hospital cashier, ask the international patient desk for three documents in English:

items: Epikriz (discharge/clinical summary): States the diagnosis, ICD-10 code, and treatment provided.
Itemised invoice (detaylı fatura): Breaks down doctor consultation, lab tests, imaging, and medications line by line.
Payment receipt and stamped prescription: Proof of settlement plus any pharmacy receipts from an external Eczane.

faq.q: Can a Turkish pharmacist refill my US, UK, or EU prescription?
faq.a: No. Turkish pharmacies can only dispense prescription-only medicines against a prescription issued by a doctor licensed in Türkiye. If you run out of a prescription drug, book a quick outpatient consultation at a private hospital to obtain a local reçete.

faq.q: Are Turkish pharmacies open on Sundays and during Bayram holidays?
faq.a: Regular pharmacies close on Sundays and public holidays, including Ramazan Bayramı and Kurban Bayramı. However, designated Nöbetçi Eczane duty pharmacies remain open 24 hours a day in every district throughout holidays.

faq.q: Do public hospitals in Türkiye treat foreign tourists in emergencies?
faq.a: Yes. Under Turkish law, state hospitals provide emergency stabilisation regardless of nationality, though English-speaking staff are far less common than at private hospitals such as American Hospital, Acıbadem, or Memorial.

faq.q: Should I call 112 or take a taxi to the hospital?
faq.a: For life-threatening symptoms—chest pain, severe trauma, breathing difficulty, or loss of consciousness—call 112 immediately. For minor fractures, high fevers, or dehydration when you can travel safely, a taxi to a private hospital's Acil department is often faster in heavy Istanbul traffic.

faq.q: How much does an outpatient ER visit cost at a private hospital in Istanbul?
faq.a: A standard emergency consultation at a top-tier private Istanbul hospital typically runs €100–€250 before labs or imaging, with transparent quotes provided upfront at the international patient desk.

faq.q: Do I need travel insurance that covers private hospitals in Türkiye?
faq.a: Yes. Your home public health plan (including the UK NHS, Canadian provincial plans, US Medicare, and EU EHIC/GHIC cards) does not cover private medical care in Türkiye, so comprehensive travel medical insurance is essential.
